description: Snowflake autocommit semantics: an explicit BEGIN suspends autocommit until COMMIT or ROLLBACK, even though autocommit is ON by default - you do NOT have to SET AUTOCOMMIT=FALSE first. BEGIN used to be auto-committed at statement end, so explicit multi-statement transactions silently did not group. Pinned: a write is visible to its own transaction before commit and discarded by ROLLBACK; COMMIT persists everything the transaction did; a ROLLBACK is atomic over MULTIPLE statements, not just the last one; without a BEGIN each statement still autocommits on its own; and the whole BEGIN-INSERT-COMMIT sequence submitted as ONE multi-statement script persists too. Converted 1:1 from transaction/ExplicitTransactionTest (now retired); it ran on the default engine, with autocommit and deferred apply both on, which is what the testkit backend gives it.
